hypotheses.note: a 1-periodic, non-constant, future causal curve of the regular de Sitter region; causal = locally in a chart, s1 <= s2 => yhat(s2) - yhat(s1) future causal or zero on the hyperboloid {Q = 1} (GX.DSLe); chart-independent (IsFutureCausalCurve.forall_chart); curves do not cross points of the singular set
a point of the singular set with some link at the apex (IsApexLink) of type space-like/light-like of degree k >= 4, or trivial holonomy delta^k, k >= 4

hypotheses.paper: the suspension e(L) of the associated circle (l.1117)
hypotheses.note: IsCausalLine quantifies over all developing data; isCausalLine_iff_exists gives the same answer for some
false for singular HS-surfaces (counterexample); proved in its 'only if' for singular lines, 'if' on 3 tagged sorrys

sorries.obstruction: space-like circles of degree k (tachyons): the developed image is all of l(p), so no Gamma_p-invariant function (B(., p), B(., n+)B(., n-)) is a time function on the region the charts reach; a time function must be built through the gluing by the hyperbolic holonomy; the paper gives no argument

trivial holonomy delta^k at p in dS^2 (k = 2: e(l(p)) = HS^2): the time function of HS^2 is not Gamma_p-invariant; transporting it chart by chart (regular_susp, or the holonomy-1 developing map of e(L)) is not formalized

an apex link of a point of the singular set is determined only up to a moved-p isomorphism by the HS-isomorphism of the singularities, with the degree invariant: the developing argument on the punctured neighbourhood left open by HSAntipodal SCOPE (b) (l.850-852), not formalized

findings: Scope imprecision (AUDIT-1 minor, reworded): l.1120-1125 ('In other words, a singular HS-surface is causal if the following singularity types are excluded: space-like or light-like singularities of degree >= 4, Misner singularities') fails when read literally for every singular HS-surface (l.948–952 asks no compactness): the regular part e(L) minus its two apices, L Misner, is a singular HS-surface without any singular point that has a closed causal curve (GX.exists_isSingularHSSurface_sing_empty_hasCCC). Having no CCC is a global condition, not implied by the local types. The sentence is true in its 'only if' direction for singular lines (GX.GammaLinkCircle.DevData.not_misner_of_isCausal, proved) and is stated for them as GX.GammaLinkCircle.isCausalLine_iff. The example is the Misner neighbourhood with its singular point cut out; closed surfaces and HS-spheres are undecided, and the intended reading is the singular-line form (isCausalLine_iff).

l.1059-1063 (the CTC of a Misner bigon) is formalized for every developing data (GX.GammaLinkCircle.DevData.hasCCC_of_misner): the CCC is the 'equator' of the bigon, the points of e(L) developed onto p-perp, and its causality is the order of one coordinate on a branch of the unit hyperbola of p-perp.

l.1120-1125 assert, without an argument, that every non-Misner line of degree <= 2 has no CCC (the proof of bbslem:CTC, l.1066-1101, only reduces CCCs of e(Sigma) to those of the de Sitter region of Sigma). It is proved here for time-like lines (every cone angle), light-like ones (cuspidal, extreme BTZ-like, photons, and in fact every degree) and BTZ-like ones; for tachyons of degree 2 and the trivial holonomy delta^2 it remains open (two tagged sorrys). Light-like lines of degree >= 4 have no CCC: only the degree clause makes them non-causal.
questions: Causal curves of a singular HS-surface: may they pass through points of the singular set (as l.1032-1033 lets AdS causal curves cross singular lines)? Read: no; they live in the regular de Sitter region.
CCC: causal or time-like (l.1059 speaks of CTCs)? Read: causal (future causal, 1-periodic, non-constant); the Misner curve constructed is in fact time-like, not stated.

'A singularity of degree >= 4': read through some link at the apex p-bar (IsApexLink); with 'every link' instead, the other direction of isCausalLine_iff would need the uniqueness of the link. Trivial holonomy delta^k, k >= 4 (outside the printed list) is counted as degree k.

'A singular line is causal if e(L) is causal': e(L) depends on developing data (OQ-126 (c)); read for every developing data, the 'for some' reading gives the same equivalence (isCausalLine_iff_exists).
'In other words' (l.1120): read for singular lines (the second sentence's e(L)); for general singular HS-surfaces it is false (finding); for HS-spheres of interactions it is not decided here.
kb_proposals: The causal relation of dS^2 in HS^2 is GX.DSLe (hyperboloid points GX.dsHat, difference future causal), SO0(1,2)-invariant (GX.dsLe_smul_iff); causal curves of a singular HS-surface are GX.SingularHSStructure.IsFutureCausalCurve, chart-independent by IsFutureCausalCurve.forall_chart.

To exclude CCCs use GX.SingularHSStructure.not_hasCCC_of_timeFunctionOn (a Gamma_p-invariant Phi on a region the charts reach) or not_hasCCC_of_lexTime (Phi weakly monotone, then a function on M); on e(L) chart invariance is suspAtlas_eventually_eq_smul plus Phi(g . sigma) = Phi sigma for g in Gamma_p.

A curve in e(L) given by heights along the covering: GX.GammaLinkCircle.DevData.bPt x = [E x, t x]; eventually_chart_bPt reads it in any cone chart as g . yPt x (the IsLiftOf + periodic.fiber + vlift_add_int argument of suspAtlas_eventually_eq_smul, packaged).
At p in dS^2, p-perp = span(GammaP.dsE0 p, jVec p) (GX.perp_decomp; dsE0 and dsFrame live in namespace GX.GammaP); GX.eq_zero_of_minkB_frame is the coordinate kernel.
Any property of the developed image of one lifted developing pair, invariant under Gamma_p, holds along every DevData: GX.GammaLinkCircle.DevData.d_mem_of_image (exists_rel + existsUnique_eq_smul).
A continuous locally injective f : R -> R is locally increasing everywhere up to a sign kappa = +-1: GX.exists_sign_strictMonoOn (clopen argument).
